diagnostic_evidence.quote: We present a closed-form solution to Wahba's problem in the quaternion domain for the special case of two vector observations.

The presented results offer a complete theoretical characterisation of the Wahba problem in quaternions and lay a rigorous foundation for further generalisations in quaternion-based orientation estimation.
Then, \eqref{eq:WAHBAS_EQUATION} has a solution if and only if $(\qa[1],\qa[2]) \sim (\qb[1], \qb[2])$.

issues.failure_explanation: Wahba's problem asks for a quaternion minimizing f(q). The formal results only give (i) a solvability criterion for f(q)=0, namely pairwise similarity, and (ii) a parametrization of the zero-cost solution set under that hypothesis. For two-observation data that is not pairwise similar (e.g. any inconsistent or noisy observations, the typical Wahba setting), the paper provides no optimizer and no closed-form solution of the minimization problem; more than two observations are outside all results. Thus 'we solve the Wahba's problem for ... ℓ = 2' and 'a complete theoretical characterisation of the Wahba problem' assert strictly more than the formal content establishes.

failure_location.quote: In this paper, we solve the Wahba's problem for the special and practically important case $\ell = 2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to state precisely that the paper characterizes all zero-cost solutions (f(q)=0) for ℓ=2 under the pairwise-similarity hypothesis, and does not solve the minimization problem for general data.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised achievement and coverage (a closed-form solution of the two-observation Wahba problem; a complete characterisation of the Wahba problem in quaternions) are unreliable; only the zero-cost, pairwise-similar, ℓ=2 regime is actually characterized.
issues.title: Prose overclaims scope: claims to solve Wahba's problem for two observations and to give a complete characterisation, but only the zero-cost pairwise-similar regime is characterized
issues.why_classification: The correction is purely one of stated scope: rewording withdraws the unsupported claim but changes no theorem, proof, or guarantee, so there is no mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Substituting \eqref{eq:PAIRWISE_SIMILARITY_PROOF_PART_1} into \eqref{eq:SUM_SIMILARITY} yields $\qq[][-1]\qa[2]\qq[] = \qb[2]$, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: In the converse direction the proof obtains, from similarity of the sums, one particular nonzero quaternion q satisfying eq:SUM_SIMILARITY. It then redefines q = q1 q2 with q2 commuting with b1 and substitutes eq:PAIRWISE_SIMILARITY_PROOF_PART_1 into eq:SUM_SIMILARITY to conclude q^{-1} a2 q = b2. But eq:SUM_SIMILARITY was established for the previously obtained quaternion, not for q1 q2: the proof never shows that some q2 in the centralizer of b1 exists making q1 q2 conjugate a1+a2 to b1+b2 (equivalently, that the componentwise conditions imply the existence of a common conjugator). This existence is the crux of the converse and is exactly the missing step. (The lemma is in fact true — a centralizer/orbit argument repairs it — but that argument is nontrivial.)

failure_location.quote: Set $\qq = \qq[1]\qq[2]$, where $\qq[2]$ is a nonzero quaternion such that $\qb[1]\qq[2] = \qq[2]\qb[1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid substitution by a contained existence argument: with b2' = q1^{-1} a2 q1, conjugation by elements of the centralizer of b1 rotates the component of Im(b2') perpendicular to Im(b1); the hypotheses b2' ∼ b2 and Re(b1 b2') = Re(b1 b2) force b2 into this orbit, so some q2 commuting with b1 satisfies q2^{-1} b2' q2 = b2, and q = q1 q2 is the required common conjugator.
issues.overall_effect: The checkable characterization of pairwise similarity (componentwise similarity plus Re(a1 a2) = Re(b1 b2) implying a common conjugator) is unestablished by the given proof. No labelled result in the paper cites this lemma, so there are no formal dependents.
issues.title: Converse of the pairwise-similarity characterization lemma is not proven: the sum-conjugator is conflated with q1 q2
issues.why_classification: The lemma is true and no formal result depends on it, but the repair requires a contained, genuinely nontrivial algebraic argument (centralizer orbit reasoning), exceeding a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims that f(q)=0 is equivalent to the two-term cross-product equation, but its proof only starts from a solution and derives the cross-product equation (the forward implication). The converse — recovering q^{-1} a2 q = b2 from the two alignment equations together with Re(a1 a2) = Re(b1 b2), which requires a cancellation argument — is never given. Consequently the proof of Theorem SOLUTION_TO_THE_HOMOGENEOUS_WAHBAS_EQUATION, which invokes this equivalence ('it equivalently holds') and then only derives the parametrized form from an arbitrary solution before ending with 'which completes the proof', establishes only necessity: every solution has the form q = q1 q2. It never verifies that the parametrized family consists of solutions, so the claimed 'general solution' is not proven as stated. (The converse is true in the generic case, so this is a proof gap, not a falsity.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the lemma's converse (from q^{-1} a1 q = b1 and q^{-1} Im(a1 a2) q = Im(b1 b2) with Re(a1 a2) = Re(b1 b2), deduce q^{-1} a1 a2 q = b1 b2 = (q^{-1} a1 q) b2 and cancel q^{-1} a1), and add to the main theorem's proof a sufficiency verification showing that every admissible parametrized q1 q2 satisfies both alignment equations and hence f(q1 q2) = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's characterization of the zero-cost solution set is only half-proven: inclusion of the solution set in the parametrized family is established, but sufficiency of the parametrization is not. (The theorem also fails outright in degenerate configurations; those are reported as separate issues.)
issues.title: Cross-product equivalence is proven only in the forward direction, so the main theorem's 'general solution' is established only as a necessity statement
issues.why_classification: All substantive claims survive in the generic case, but the repair must add a missing implication to the lemma and the entire missing sufficiency direction to the main theorem's proof — a contained but nontrivial completion rather than a routine local edit.

Nonreal quaternions $\qa,\qb$ are called similar if there exists a nonzero quaternion $\qp$ such that $\qp[][-1]\qa\qp = \qb$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow collinear data: Im(a1) parallel to Im(a2) (then also Im(b1) parallel to Im(b2), since |a1×a2| = |b1×b2| follows from pairwise similarity). In that case a3 = q1^{-1}(a1×a2)q1 = 0 and b3 = b1×b2 = 0, so the radicand in the q2-formula is 0 — which is moreover outside Lemma QUATERNION_SQRT, stated for a nonzero quaternion — forcing q2 = λ2·√0 = 0 and hence q = q1 q2 = 0, an inadmissible quaternion (its inverse is undefined). The parametrization therefore produces no valid quaternion at all, although the solution set is nonempty: e.g. a1=i, a2=2i, b1=j, b2=2j are pairwise similar and every q with q^{-1} i q = j solves f(q)=0. The proof fails exactly where Theorem NONZERO_SOLUTIONS_OF_THE_HOMOGENEOUS_SYLVESTER_EQUATION — stated for similar, hence by Definition SIMILAR_QUATERNIONS nonreal, quaternions — is applied to a3 = b3 = 0, which are real: for a3 = b3 = 0 every nonzero q2 solves a3 q2 = q2 b3, but the cited formula yields only q2 = 0, so the invoked conclusion fails precisely where it is used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a non-collinearity hypothesis (Im(a1)×Im(a2) ≠ 0, equivalently Im(b1)×Im(b2) ≠ 0) to the theorem and handle the collinear case separately, where the solution set is the full two-parameter family {q : q^{-1} a1 q = b1}, already described by the q1-formula via the cited Sylvester theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed closed-form parametrization of all zero-cost quaternions is false in the collinear two-observation regime, which is covered by the theorem's hypotheses; there the theorem delivers no solutions at all.
issues.title: Main theorem fails for collinear observations: the q2-formula collapses to zero and the entire solution set is missed
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated in an in-scope degenerate regime, but a case split with a trivial separate treatment of the collinear case preserves the method, the generic result, and the advertised contribution without new proof architecture or major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Suppose a3 = -b3 ≠ 0, i.e. q1^{-1}(Im(a1)×Im(a2))q1 = -(b1×b2). Then the radicand a3 b3* is negative real, so its square roots are arbitrary pure directions, which need not commute with b1 even though eq:HOMOGENEOUS_SOLUTION_PROOF_PART_1 requires [q2, b1] = 0. The proof's final computation '0 = q2 b1 - b1 q2 = μ2(...)' silently discards the commutator of the λ2 √(a3 b3*) term with b1; this inference is valid only when a3 ≠ -b3. The theorem's second side condition does not repair the omission: (i) its trigger 'q1*(Im(a1)×Im(a2))q1 = -(Im(b1)×Im(b2))' is misscaled, since q1* = |q1|² q1^{-1}, so unless |q1| = 1 it never fires and no constraint is imposed at all; (ii) even when it fires, orthogonality of Im(q2) to a3 is strictly weaker than the actual requirement q2 parallel to Im(b1) (commutation with b1 combined with anticommutation with a3). Counterexample: a1=i, a2=j, b1=j, b2=i are pairwise similar; with q1=(1-k)/√2 the parametrization admits q2 ∝ i (the stated side condition holds, k·i=0), giving q ∝ (i-j)/√2, for which q^{-1} i q = -j ≠ b1 and f(q)=4≠0. With |q1|≠1 the trigger does not fire and, e.g., q2 ∝ k yields q ∝ 1+k with q^{-1} i q = -j, again a non-solution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the second side condition: state the trigger with the properly scaled quantity q1^{-1}(Im(a1)×Im(a2))q1 = -(b1×b2) (or absorb the |q1|² factor), and in that case replace the constraint by the correct one, e.g. q2 = t·Im(b1) with t ≠ 0; equivalently, re-derive the constraint from [q2, b1] = 0, which the λ2-term does not automatically satisfy when a3 = -b3.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact characterization of the zero-cost solution set is false whenever the free parameter q1 makes a3 = -b3: the parametrized family then contains quaternions that do not solve Wahba's equation, so the 'general solution' overincludes.
issues.title: Main theorem includes non-solutions when the conjugated cross-products are antiparallel: dropped commutator term and misscaled, insufficient side condition
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated in an in-scope degenerate configuration, but the repair is a contained correction of one side condition together with the corresponding proof step, preserving the generic result, the method, and the advertised contribution.
